issues.description: Method name mismatch: The problem statement UML and the solution implementation define a Stock method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient). The template repository's Stock class instead provides a method named addItem(StockIngredient). This naming inconsistency means code (e.g., SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery) written to call addToStockIngredients will not compile against the template, and students following the UML will be confused which method to implement or use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template match the problem statement and solution: rename the template method Stock.addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient). Alternatively, add a new method addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) in the template that delegates to the existing addItem to preserve compatibility, or update the UML/problem statement and solution to consistently use addItem across all artifacts.

issues.description: Concept: adding a StockIngredient to the Stock collection. Problem statement / UML and the solution implement a method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) for Stock. The template Stock implementation instead provides a method named addItem(StockIngredient). A student reading the UML/problem will look for addToStockIngredients in the template but will find addItem, making it unclear which method to call and how to implement SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery to add new StockIngredient objects.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across artifacts. Rename the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) so the template matches the UML/problem statement and the solution. Alternatively, update the UML/problem statement and the solution to use addItem, but the preferred fix is to align the template with the problem/UML by renaming addItem to addToStockIngredients.
